messages:
maria_support: customer in Frankfurt reports intermittent 401s and 300-800ms token latency since ~08:30 CET. says some requests land in us-east based on logs. can we confirm routing?

kevin_netops: can you paste a sample request_id and a client ip (best-effort)? also any dig/trace from their network?

maria_support: request_id=req_0a9f6b2c, client_ip=185.12.34.56. asked customer to run `dig +short @8.8.8.8 api.redwood.com` — they returned `52.204.12.77` (us-east). they said their ISP resolver TTL is 60s but customer still sees us-east for >20min.

irene_sre: hm, sounds like resolver cache + EDNS stripping or ISP NAT. NAT64 can flip country code. did they provide `dig +trace` or `curl -v`? can we see edge logs for that request_id?

maria_support: pasted curl headers from customer: `GET /v1/generate` -> 401 with `x-edge-pop: iad1` and `x-request-latency-ms: 312`. edge logs show `pop=iad1` for that req.

kevin_netops: good. likely geoip DB mapped their resolver's visible IP to US or upstream resolver returning stale anycast answer. ask customer to `dig +short @1.1.1.1 api.redwood.com` and `dig +short api.redwood.com` from their machine to compare. also ask them to `dig +edns=0` to see EDNS behavior.

maria_support: customer ran tests: `@8.8.8.8` -> 52.204.12.77, `@1.1.1.1` -> 52.204.12.77, `local` -> 52.204.12.77. they also sent `traceroute` — first hop shows ISP CGNAT (10.x.x.x), then transit to `93.184.200.1` then us-east path.

andre_devex: CGNAT + ISP resolver likely returning stale cached A record. TTL of authoritative is 20s but many ISPs ignore short TTLs. also possible EDNS-client-subnet stripped by ISP. if EDNS is stripped, our geolocation may fall back to resolver IP (which could be in US).

irene_sre: can infra check our GeoIP DB entry for that resolver IP (52.204.12.77)? and check if S3 sync for geodb had any errors in last hour. ops-bot can you surface last geodb sync status?

ops-bot: geodb-sync: last successful sync 2026-03-17T06:12:02Z. recent sync jobs: 0 failures in last 24h. manual reload scheduled? no.

kevin_netops: thanks. since geodb looks current, two hypotheses: 1) ISP resolver in the path is actually in US (so mapping is correct) 2) upstream resolver returning anycast answer from US due to ISP peering. both cause user traffic to reach iad1.

maria_support: customer asks what they can do now — they expect EU pop. any quick mitigations?

andre_devex: short-term: ask them to switch to a local recursive that preserves EDNS (if possible) or have them test via a VPN to EU to confirm app behavior. we can also temporarily adjust routing policy for that customer (pin to eu-central model variant) but needs ProdEng approval + risk assessment.

irene_sre: also recommend purge of our edge DNS cache for that hostname in case stale delegation exists: `aws cloudfront create-invalidation --paths \"/api.redwood.com/*\"` (example) — but note most of this is resolver-side.

kevin_netops: repro steps for support notes: 1) collect `dig +short` from 3 resolvers (8.8.8.8, 1.1.1.1, local), 2) `dig +trace`, 3) `traceroute -n api.redwood.com` or `tracepath`, 4) paste edge headers (`x-edge-pop`, `x-request-id`, `x-auth-status`). attach those to ticket.

maria_support: customer provided dig+trace and traceroute. i've attached to ticket (#INC-2026-867). requesting temporary pin to eu-central while customer escalates with ISP.

irene_sre: i'll approve a temporary routing override for that customer id (tenant=acme-inc) to prefer eu-central pop for 2 hours. ops-bot will apply after kevin signs off.

kevin_netops: signing off. ops-bot, apply routing override: tenant=acme-inc, prefer_pops=[fra1,ams1], ttl=7200s.

ops-bot: routing-override: request accepted. applying now... done. new requests for tenant acme-inc should prefer FRA/AMS for next 7200s. :white_check_mark:

andre_devex: follow-up: ask infra to add a healthcheck to detect long-lived cross-region answers from resolvers for anycast zones (alert when >2% of queries from EU customers resolve to non-EU pops for >10 min). filing infra ticket.

maria_support: thanks all — i'll update customer that we've pinned them to EU pops and provided troubleshooting steps they can try with ISP. closing interim slack thread, will reopen if issue reappears. :thumbsup:
